notes: The whole fragment is one continuous floor speech that begins before the stretch and continues past its end; the markup contains no run at all, so there is no label to record and no turn starts here. Checking the wider file (data/raw/senado/taquigraficas/2002-02-21_r83_ORDINARIA.html), the last label before the fragment is 'Sr. Alfonsín. --', and the next label comes well after the fragment ends, which confirms a single uninterrupted turn. This is live floor speech, not an inserted document: it is addressed to the chair ('señor presidente') throughout and contains a personal aside about the speaker's own pension. EVENTS: empty, and deliberately so. The fragment contains two parenthesised laughter notes, typeset inconsistently: the first is printed '(Risas.)' with the parentheses outside the italic run ('(Risas.)'), the second is printed '(risas).' lowercase, with the parentheses inside the italic run and the full stop OUTSIDE the closing parenthesis ('(risas).'). I first listed both as events. Both are now excluded, because both sit INLINE inside a paragraph of the senator's own speech, with his words running on either side of them: '...correligionarios y colegas--. (Risas.) Creo que esto es lo urgente.' and '...fue lo de la vejez (risas). Y que además de esa jubilación...'. Under the corpus convention (TODO.md, Phase 2: 'inline italic fragments merged back into speech instead of splitting turns'; the PDF side has a block type `inline_italic` for exactly this) an event is a note printed as its OWN paragraph. Neither of these is. NOTE THE REASON: they are not being judged unreal or mistranscribed - the stenographer did record laughter both times, and a reader of the page sees it. They are reclassified as part of the surrounding speech because of WHERE they are printed, not because of what they say. If the convention is ever revisited so that inline notes count, this fragment has two of them and this file will need re-emitting. Two other italic runs in this fragment are NOT stenographer's notes and were excluded on a different and stronger ground: 'post mortem' and 'staff', both italicised simply as foreign-language words inside the senator's sentences. Those are not notes at all, at any position on the page. That is the same distinction as the one above drawn one level finer: italics alone do not make an event, and a real note inline does not make one either. Adjacent case a maintainer may want to rule on, OUTSIDE this fragment so not recorded here: immediately after the stretch ends the sitting prints '...seguimos siendo pobres, señor presidente. (Aplausos.)' - a note in a third position, paragraph-FINAL rather than mid-sentence or standalone. It is not covered cleanly by either reading of the convention.
